knowledge_point.title: Solving a System of Equations by Eliminating the Second Variable

question.:question/problem:
Find the solution $(x, y)$ to the following system of equations using the elimination method:
$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x-21y&=-40\\-5x-3y&=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

*Hint: Eliminate the variable $y$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the $y$-coefficient in the first equation is $-21$, while in the second equation it is $-3$.

If we multiply the second equation by $-7$, then the $y$-coefficient will become $21$, which will cancel with the coefficient of $-21$ in the first equation.

$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $y$ will be eliminated:

$$

35x+21y&=7 \\

33x&=-33 \\
x&=-1
\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $x = -1$. However, we still need to find $y$. To do this, we substitute $x = -1$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the second equation:

$$

\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is
